stem: Pointing to a photograph, Meena says, 'He is the only son of my father's father.' How is the person in the photograph related to Meena?

per_option_rationale.rationale: Meena's father's father is her grandfather. The only son of her grandfather is her father. So the person is Meena's father.
Treating 'father's father' as one generation up (i.e. treating father's father as if he were father's brother) incorrectly gives uncle.
Mistakenly associating 'father's father' directly with the person asked about rather than with the person whose son is being described gives grandfather.
Forgetting the clue specifies 'only son' and instead linking the same generation to Meena gives brother - ignoring the generation step through grandfather.

explanation: Meena's father's father = grandfather. Grandfather's only son = Meena's father. Therefore the person in the photograph is Meena's father.

explanation_sections.punchline: Two-step chain: grandfather's only son is the father, not the grandfather himself and not a sibling.
explanation_sections.approach: Apply clues most-certain-first: identify the reference person (Meena's father's father = grandfather), then identify the target (only son of grandfather = father). The chain has two links, both must be traversed.
explanation_sections.lesson: Always traverse every link in the description chain; stopping one link short places the answer at the wrong generation.
explanation_sections.timing: Under 50 s. Trap is option 3 (grandfather) - it stops after the first link; option 2 (uncle) comes from treating the second link as a sibling instead of a child.
